stances_toward.note: NATO and EU co-member (Art. 5, Art. 42(7)) and the biggest source of goods after Germany and Italy (12.0% of imports, 11.8% of exports in 2025); Plenkovic credits Slovenia's support for euro and Schengen entry. The border dispute is parked, not solved: Slovenia treats the 2017 Piran Bay arbitration award as binding, Croatia calls the process null and its parliament rejected it; the two prime ministers agreed in 2023 to keep it out of daily politics and signed a border-bridges agreement on 23 Jun 2025. Slovenia's new government under Janez Jansa (confirmed 22 May 2026) is right-of-centre but no 2026 statement on the border was found. Hand-written because the derived ally stance has no bond or trend. Bond - affinity: shared history and a common Schengen frontier.

relations_to.summary: The Piran Bay and land border are unsettled. The 2017 arbitration award gave Slovenia most of the bay and a junction to the high seas; Croatia withdrew from the process in 2015 and does not implement the award. In 2023 the two prime ministers agreed to keep the dispute out of daily politics.

the proceedings were contaminated and the award null; the Sabor rejected it entirely (Plenkovic, July 2023)
